title: Exact localization and normalization data for ambient clopen comparisons
statement: On small pro-etale sheaf categories and simultaneous ringed sequence-site module categories, define localize of an exact natural transformation by termwise application and Localization.liftNatTrans. Define localizeSquare by inverse source and forward target exact-composition isomorphisms. The restrictionNormalized predicate is the identity restriction equation R(η) σ K(a)=v; sheafNormalized specializes it to the ordinary open units and pullback square isomorphism, and Normalized specializes to finite constant coefficient modules. Define derivedAlpha by localizeSquare of the ordinary alpha with the canonical total/exact inverse-image transports. AdjunctionOnComplexes records the localized unit and counit equations on QK. Systems.Normalized and Systems.Assertion record the same equations and comparisons on entire systems; OrdinaryAssertion records their sheaf versions. transportAlpha is the composite of four specified functor isomorphisms around a square transformation. realizationAlpha specializes it to the canonical bridge. All constructions use the specified data of [def-sf-ambient-underived-clopen-comparison], [def-sp-varying-ring-proper-open-arrows], [def-sf-semilinear-proper-open-comparisons], [def-sf-integral-system-canonical-bridge], [def-sf-integral-system-operations] and [def-sf-integral-system-realization-data]. No existence theorem is used to choose a new comparison. The ordinary beta, clopen projector, open compositors and alpha are constructed over any Grothendieck abelian coefficient category and then specialized to ModuleCat; their formulas are unchanged. The two proved projection equations for the named squareLift retain that name instead of requiring clients to unfold the scheme pullback. For categories A, B, C, D, adjunctions a:L1 ⊣ R1 and b:L2 ⊣ R2, functors G:A→C and H:B→D, a square α:G⋙L2→L1⋙H, a transformation γ:R1⋙G→H⋙R2 and M:B, properMateFormula is exactly γ.app M = b.unit.app (G.obj (R1.obj M)) ≫ R2.map (α.app (R1.obj M)) ≫ R2.map (H.map (a.counit.app M)). This is the same mate component equation, with its category data retained as explicit parameters.
